newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MILLING WHEAT UP, OTHER GRAINS DOWN IN BUDAPEST.
newsitem.headline: MILLING WHEAT UP, OTHER GRAINS DOWN IN BUDAPEST.

text.p: Milling and euro wheat futures prices went limit-up on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Friday, while most other grains finished lower in low turnover.
Grains futures turnover on the BCE dropped to a meagre 425 lots or 188.1 million forints compared with the week's total (Friday included) of 3,995 lots or 1.8 billion forints.
Traders said milling wheat futures were likely to continue to rise as the market's fears of a low quality wheat crop were being confirmed.
"Some August deliveries seem to be doubtful or at least very difficult to honour," said Robert Vajo of Termin brokerage.
Persistent rains in June and July are said to have lowered the quality of the wheat crop in both gluten content and starch to sugar ratio.

Milling wheat prices rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all maturities in token turnover and three maturities, September 1997, January and September 1998 will be freed up on Monday as they rose by limit for three consecutive days.

The Budapest Commodity Exchange frees up any maturity from limit movements after three consecutive days of limit move in either direction. The limit is set back once the daily price change remains within 400 forints per tonne.
Two euro wheat maturities, August 1998 and September 1998, were freed up on Friday and surged 850 and 810 forints per tonne to 25,200 and 26,010 forints, respectively.
Most other euro wheat maturities went limit-up and will be freed up on Monday except January 1999, which only rose 300 forints to 28,000.
Vajo said that with delivery times far away for euro wheat, which was introduced one week ago, there was virtually no information to trade on.
"But I think the rise will stop when prices reach a level where producers start to open speculative selling positions," he said.

Feed wheat prices went limit-down for most maturities on abundant supply and the lack of export opportunities and two maturities, January and May will be freed up on Monday after other three, October, December and March were freed up today.
Barley prices finished lower for all but steady September on profit-taking after days of rises, Vajo said.

Dormant sunflower seed prices showed the first signs of revival going limit-down for December and Vajo said that with sunflower harvesting due to start in a month's time, it was slowly getting more attention.

"The domestic oil industry pays about 39,000 forints per tonne plus quality premium for sunflower seed and BCE prices are better than that, and there is a quality premium system on the BCE as well," he said.
Sunflower seed prices settled between 44,250 forints for September and 44,650 for December with a slight inverse spread as November stood at 44,800 forints.
Maize futures finished steady to lower in minimal turnover.
